verdict.line: You lose lane if you facecheck his Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo or farm low-health near a level-6 Feast; you win the 55.9% of games where you survive the early CC chain and out-scale him with raw HP.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's entire kit is burst on cooldowns (Q 9s, W 13s, R 60s) with no sustained pressure between casts, while Mundo's Adrenaline Rush passive and percent-health Q (Infected Cleaver) punish exactly that kind of all-or-nothing trading. The matchup is even on paper per OP.GG, but the 261-game sample skews 55.9% to Mundo because Cho's biggest risk window is a single true-damage Feast at level 6, and everything after that is a war of attrition Mundo's kit is built to win.

theirWindow.when: Right after Rupture lands on you
theirWindow.what: He'll chain W (Feral Scream) for the silence and magic damage immediately after Rupture's slow lands, and from level 6 on he can follow that combo with R (Feast) true damage if you're already low. Back off minion aggro the instant Rupture clips you until you know his W and R are down.

yourWindow.when: Once his Q and W are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With Rupture (9s) and Feral Scream (13s) spent, he has no disengage or follow-up CC for several seconds. Walk in, hold W (Burning Agony) active for the continual damage and disable-duration reduction, and poke with Q (Infected Cleaver) — he can't punish it.

start.why: The passive block and extra regen cushion the free poke damage from Rupture and Vorpal Spikes while you're still one-item, and it's the stronger of the two listed starts at 57.4% over 209 games.

boots.why: The 58.3% win rate over 199 games reflects how much the extra movement speed matters for stepping out of Rupture's landing zone and closing distance once his Q and W are down.

core.why: Raw max-health scales Adrenaline Rush's percent-health regen directly and blunts how much Feast's true damage can take off you in one hit.
Continues stacking max health for the same Adrenaline Rush and Feast-survival reasons; this path hits 60.5% over 38 games.
Converts the HP you've stacked into real trading damage so you're not just a wall once he's out of cooldowns to burst you.

situational.when: his rupture and feral scream chip are adding up faster than you can regen
the enemy team has heavy auto-attack or crit damage alongside cho'gath
the enemy backline is stacking lifesteal or sustained auto damage

runes.keystoneWhy: Every proc heals you back off your max health, which stacks directly with Adrenaline Rush and offsets the chip damage from his cooldown rotation during the levels he has lane initiative.

summoners.why: This is the most-picked combo at 50.6% pick rate with a 53.6% win rate — Teleport lets you reset after shoving a wave past his Rupture zone, and Ghost closes the gap to punish him the moment his Q and W are both on cooldown.

playing.title: Bait Rupture before trading
playing.detail: Hold your Q poke until he throws Rupture (9s cooldown) at a minion or whiffs it on you. Once it's down you have a clean window to walk in since his follow-up Feral Scream (13s cooldown) has no setup slow to land with.

playing.title: Hold W through the silence
playing.detail: If Rupture clips you and Feral Scream silences you right after, your active W (Burning Agony) keeps dealing its continual damage and still reduces the disable's duration — don't panic back off just because you're silenced.

playing.title: Trade through Vorpal Spikes, don't flinch
playing.detail: His auto attacks proc Vorpal Spikes on a 0.5s cooldown with no bait-and-punish window — it's constant chip. Out-sustain it with Adrenaline Rush and your own Q poke rather than disengaging from it.

playing.title: Respect the level-6 Feast threat
playing.detail: From level 6 on, don't sit below roughly half health while farming. Feast is true damage at 175 range on a 60s cooldown and can delete a low-health Mundo who's not paying attention.

playing.title: Punish with E after you tank the combo
playing.detail: Masochism (7s cooldown) scales your attack damage off missing health, so right after you've eaten his Rupture-Feral Scream combo is often your hardest-hitting moment — turn and fight rather than retreat.

playing.title: Play for the scaling, not the early kill
playing.detail: Solo-kill numbers favor Cho'Gath early, so don't force all-ins before level 6. The 55.9% win rate over 261 games comes from outscaling him with HP itemization, not from winning the first few levels.

playing.title: Save R to survive, not to start fights
playing.detail: Sadism (75s cooldown) trades health for movement speed and heavy regen. Save it to stabilize or disengage after he dumps his full combo into you, rather than popping it to initiate.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — cooldown windows, trade patterns, and the level-6 Feast warning — is my own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of his (Q) as he can chain his abilities afterwards. After reaching level 6, be careful of being nuked by (R) while farming lane.
